race.name: Reliance Tennessee Gravel
race.tagline: Eight thousand feet of climbing through Cherokee National Forest in 70 miles.

vitals.registration: Online only. Saturday entry: $75-$105; registration closes April 18, 2027.
vitals.prize_purse: More than $2,000 across the weekend's three race distances
vitals.aid_stations: Four stocked aid stations on the 70-mile route at miles 15, 27, 44, and 55
vitals.cutoff_time: No rider cutoff; aid stations and sweep support have closing times

climate.description: A late-April mountain race where variable conditions can change the grip and speed of the forest roads.
challenges: Long exposed effort if support closes

terrain.surface: The 70-mile route is 60% gravel, with chunky forest roads, curving pavement, punchy grades, and steep, rutted descending from Starr Mountain.
features: Powerhouse, McFarland, Buck Bald, Fingerboard, and Starr Mountain

gravel_god_rating.score_note: A well-supported grassroots weekend with exceptional climbing and strong value, held back from destination status by remote logistics, an unmarked course, and limited field depth.

biased_opinion.summary: Reliance is a compact but serious mountain-gravel race: 8,100 feet in 70 miles, 60% gravel, four stocked aid stations, and an unmarked route through Cherokee National Forest. The small field and remote base keep it regional, but the support, included food, live music, camping, and technical course give it more substance than the old profile suggested.
strengths: Named climbs and technical descending in Cherokee National Forest
Four stocked aid stations plus sweep support
Included post-race food, music, beer, and camping options
weaknesses: Remote location with limited nearby lodging and dining
No course marking; GPS navigation is mandatory
Aid-station and sweep coverage closes before the final rider cutoff
Chunky and rutted descents punish weak handling
biased_opinion.bottom_line: One of the better-value climbing weekends in the Southeast. Travel for the course and the camp atmosphere, not for a deep national field or polished big-event logistics.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 70-mile climber's course with 8,100 feet, chunky forest gravel, and a full grassroots weekend around it.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a hard, technical climbing day and can navigate an unmarked course. Skip it if you need easy travel, frequent town access, or a national-caliber field.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a larger destination field, consider Gravel Worlds. For another climbing-heavy Southeast event, consider Hot Springs Gravel Gauntlet.

logistics.airport: Chattanooga (CHA); verify ground-transfer time before booking
logistics.lodging_strategy: Reserve a campsite at Hiwassee Outfitters with registration or stay in a larger nearby town; Reliance itself has limited inventory.
logistics.food: Post-ride lunch is included Saturday and Sunday; breakfast and dinner are sold on site during listed windows.
logistics.packet_pickup: Friday 3:00-8:00 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday 6:00-8:00 a.m. at Hiwassee Outfitters
logistics.parking: Free at Hiwassee Outfitters; the adjacent boat ramp is not event parking
logistics.camping: Free first-come space is limited; reservable primary campsites are available through registration

history.origin_story: A grassroots race-and-ride weekend built around Cherokee National Forest routes and a Hiwassee Outfitters base camp.
history.reputation: A small, climbing-heavy Southern Blue Ridge gravel weekend.

course_description.character: Relentless Southern Blue Ridge climbing on a 60% gravel loop, with chunky forest roads, fast pavement, and a steep final mountain descent.

suffering_zones.label: McFarland
suffering_zones.desc: The opening river section and Powerhouse climbing feed into the first stocked aid station at the top of McFarland.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Scenic river start, gravel climbing, then a fast descent

suffering_zones.label: Buck Bald
suffering_zones.desc: A five-mile climb reaches the Buck Bald checkpoint before the punchy Fingerboard section.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Sustained climb followed by rolling, steep gravel

suffering_zones.label: Starr Mountain
suffering_zones.desc: The final major climb reaches the last stocked aid station, then turns into a steep and rutted descent before two smaller finishing climbs.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Five-mile mountain climb and high-consequence descent

course_description.signature_challenge: Arriving at Starr Mountain with enough climbing strength and handling precision to manage its steep, rutted descent after 55 miles.

guide_variables.race_terrain: 60% gravel with chunky forest roads, sustained climbs, and steep mountain descents
guide_variables.race_weather: Variable late-April Southern Blue Ridge conditions
race_challenges: Aid and sweep support closing times

non_negotiables.why: The long race packs 8,100 feet into 70 miles, with Starr Mountain still waiting after mile 50.
The Starr Mountain descent begins steep and rutted, after most of the day's climbing is already in the legs.
The route is unmarked, missed turns are specifically flagged, and late riders may outlast aid-station and sweep coverage.

migration_notes: 2027 long-race date, route, schedule, pricing, support, and logistics verified against official organizer pages on 2026-08-06

topics.pacing: Protecting the final climb and descent across 8,100 feet of vertical gain
topics.climbing: Powerhouse, Buck Bald, Fingerboard, and Starr Mountain effort management
topics.fueling: Using four aid stations without depending on support after its closing times
topics.navigation: Racing an unmarked GPS route through easy-to-miss forest turns

marketplace_variables.race_hook: 8,100 feet of climbing through Cherokee National Forest in 70 miles.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: A 60% gravel, unmarked climber's course with chunky roads and a steep Starr Mountain descent.

logistics.explanation: The Hiwassee Outfitters base keeps parking, packet pickup, camping, and every race start together. Reliance remains a remote, low-inventory destination, though, and the free camping area is limited enough that riders should reserve a primary campsite or arrange lodging early.

length.explanation: The flagship Saturday race is 70 miles, squarely in the system's 60-100-mile band. A separate 46-mile race on Saturday and 28-mile race on Sunday broaden the weekend without changing the long-course grade.

technicality.explanation: The organizer describes chunky forest sections, missed-turn hazards, and a steep, rutted opening on the Starr Mountain descent. It is still designed to be rideable on a gravel bike, so the handling demand is meaningful rather than mountain-bike extreme.

elevation.explanation: The official 70-mile route lists 8,100 feet of climbing, which lands in the 6,000-10,000-foot score-four band. Powerhouse, Buck Bald, Fingerboard, and Starr Mountain distribute that climbing across almost the entire race.

climate.explanation: The race runs in late April in the Southern Blue Ridge. Weather is a preparation variable because wet conditions can change the forest surfaces, but the official event materials do not frame climate as the course's defining obstacle.

altitude.explanation: Buck Bald and Starr Mountain create serious vertical gain without turning the event into a high-altitude race. The physiological challenge is repeated climbing, not thin air.

adventure.explanation: A remote base camp, an unmarked route, Cherokee National Forest roads, and a full three-day ride-and-race schedule create a complete adventure weekend. The stocked aid stations and sweep vehicles keep it below a self-supported expedition grade.

prestige.explanation: The 250-rider cap and regional organizer footprint make Reliance a recognized local and Southeast event rather than a national calendar anchor. Its appeal is the course and community, not series points or elite status.

race_quality.explanation: The 2027 event has exact schedules, separate race starts and podiums, timing, four stocked long-course aid stations, checkpoints, sweep and mechanical support, and published closing times. The deliberate lack of course marking and finite support window keep the organization good rather than professional-grade.

experience.explanation: The race day is surrounded by included lunch, beer, live music, games, a campfire afterparty, bike wash, demos, and on-site camping. Paired with the Buck Bald view and serious course, that is a memorable weekend rather than a start-ride-leave event.

community.explanation: The small field, shared base camp, two evenings of music, volunteer-led support, and proceeds benefiting SORBA Chattanooga create a strong regional community. It lacks the scale or long-established mythology required for a higher cultural grade.

field_depth.explanation: Cash prizes, nine categories, and separate podiums provide real racing, but a 250-rider cap split across multiple distances cannot produce the depth of a major national event. Expect competitive regional riders rather than a stacked professional field.

value.explanation: Saturday registration runs $75-$105 and includes timing, four stocked aid stations, sweep and mechanical support, lunch, beer, live music, and event swag. That is strong value even before the two-day registration discount.

expenses.explanation: A Southeast rider can drive, park free, camp at the venue, and eat the included post-race meal, keeping a practical weekend within the reasonable-cost band. Flying in or choosing scarce local lodging can raise the total, so it is not universally budget-grade.

rider_intel.search_text: The Reliance Tennessee gravel race features challenging terrain including dangerous bridge sections where crashes resulting in concussions and shoulder injuries have occurred. The course includes sustained climbs with 7% grades where riders slow to 7 miles per hour. Surface conditions can be hazardous, particularly tar sections that become slick when wet. The Web Brothers store serves as a key landmark and appears to be the only store in the area, making it an important logistical point. Riders are using Continental tubeless tires in 28mm widths for the varied terrain. The scenic route passes through beautiful areas that are popular with motorcycles and connects to areas like Cage Cove. The challenging nature of the course requires careful attention to technical descents and sustained climbing efforts.
